data.title: REG - Spire Healthcare Grp - Recommended Final* Acquisition
data.description:
RNS Number : 0978E Spire Healthcare Group PLC 20 November 2026  

NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION IN WHOLE OR IN PART, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY IN, INTO OR FROM ANY RESTRICTED JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OR REGULATIONS OF THAT JURISDICTION

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

20 November 2026

Recommended Final* Acquisition

of

Spire Healthcare Group plc (“Spire”)

by

Tulip UK Bidco Limited (“Bidco”)

(a newly formed company indirectly owned by a consortium including: (i) funds managed or advised by Toscafund Asset Management LLP; (ii) funds managed or advised by THCP Advisory Limited; and (iii) funds managed or advised by Ares Management Limited)

to be implemented by means of a Scheme of Arrangement under Part 26 of the Companies Act 2006

UPDATE ON SATISFACTION OF CONDITIONS AND TIMETABLE

On 5 September 2026, the Spire Directors and Bidco Board announced that they had reached agreement on the terms of a recommended final* cash offer, pursuant to which Bidco will acquire the entire issued and to be issued ordinary share capital of Spire that the Consortium does not already own (the “Acquisition”). The Acquisition is intended to be effected by means of a Court approved scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the Companies Act 2006 (the “Scheme”). Full details of the Scheme are set out in the scheme document published on 29 September 2026 (the “Scheme Document”).

As announced by Spire on 30 October 2026, the Scheme was approved by the requisite majority of Scheme Shareholders at the Court Meeting held on 30 October 2026 and the Resolution relating to the implementation of the Scheme was approved by the requisite majority of Spire Shareholders at the General Meeting also held on 30 October 2026.

* The financial terms of the Cash Offer and the Alternative Offer are final. Bidco may not revise the Cash Offer or the Alternative Offer other than in exceptional circumstances and only with the prior consent of the Panel. Bidco reserves the right to elect to implement the Acquisition by way of a Takeover Offer as an alternative to the Scheme, subject to obtaining the consent of the Panel and subject to the terms of the Co-operation Agreement.

Satisfaction of FCA Regulatory Condition

Spire and Bidco are pleased to confirm that, on 19 November 2026, the FCA Regulatory Condition set out in paragraph 3(a) of Part A of Part III of the Scheme Document was satisfied.

Completion of the Acquisition remains subject to the satisfaction (or, where applicable, waiver) of the remaining Conditions set out in the Scheme Document, including the sanction of the Scheme by the Court at the Court Hearing and the delivery of a copy of the Court Order to the Registrar of Companies.

Next steps and timetable

An updated expected timetable of remaining principal events for the implementation of the Scheme is set out below. Spire and Bidco confirm that the Court Hearing has been scheduled to be held on 3 December 2026. Details of the Court Hearing will be available on the Business and Property Division Rolls Building Daily Cause List at www.court-tribunal-hearings.service.gov.uk on the day before the Court Hearing.

Subject to the Scheme receiving the sanction of the Court at the Court Hearing, the Effective Date for the Acquisition is expected to be 7 December 2026. The last day of dealings in, and for registration of transfers of, Spire Shares on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange is expected to be on 4 December 2026, with all dealings in Spire Shares being suspended by 7.30 a.m. on 7 December 2026. It is also expected that the admission to trading of Spire Shares on the Main Market and listing of Spire Shares on the Official List will each be cancelled by 8.00 a.m. on 8 December 2026.

These dates and times are based on Spire’s and Bidco’s current expectations and are subject to change. If any of the dates and/or times in the expected timetable change, the revised dates and/or times will be notified to Spire Shareholders by announcement through a Regulatory Information Service, with such announcement being made available on Spire’s website at www.investors.spirehealthcare.com and Bidco’s website at www.toscafund.com.

Elections for the Alternative Offer

The Election Return Time, being the latest time for delivering the Form of Election (for certificated holders) or settlement of TTE Instructions (for CREST holders) in respect of the Alternative Offer, will be 1.00 p.m. on 2 December 2026, being the Business Day prior to the Court Hearing.

The KYC Return Time, being the latest time for submitting KYC Information in respect of the Alternative Offer in a form satisfactory to Bidco, will be 1.00 p.m. on 30 November 2026, being the third Business Day prior to the Court Hearing.

Following this announcement, Euroclear will be instructed to set up an appropriate event in CREST. Once the event has been set up in CREST, Eligible Scheme Shareholders who hold Spire Shares in uncertificated form and wish to elect for the Alternative Offer will be able to do so electronically by submitting (or procuring the submission of) appropriate TTE Instructions in accordance with the procedure set out in Part VI of the Scheme Document.

Eligible Scheme Shareholders who hold Spire Shares in certificated form and wish to elect for the Alternative Offer should complete and return the Form of Election in accordance with the instructions printed thereon and the procedure set out in Part VI of the Scheme Document.

The attention of Eligible Scheme Shareholders who wish to elect for the Alternative Offer is drawn to the full terms and conditions of the Alternative Offer set out in the Scheme Document, including the requirement to provide KYC Information in a form satisfactory to Bidco prior to the KYC Return Time.

Shareholders who wish to receive cash for all the Scheme Shares that they hold at the Scheme Record Time (i.e. who do not wish to make an election for the Alternative Offer) should not return the Form of Election or make a TTE Instruction.

Capitalised terms used but not defined in this announcement have the meanings given to them in Part XII of the Scheme Document.

Additional information for US investors

The Acquisition relates to the shares of an English company and is being made by means of a scheme of arrangement provided for under English law. A transaction implemented by means of a scheme of arrangement is not subject to the tender offer rules or the proxy solicitation rules under the US Exchange Act. The Acquisition is subject to the disclosure requirements and practices applicable to a scheme of arrangement involving a target company in England whose shares are traded on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange, which differ from the disclosure requirements of the US tender offer and proxy solicitation rules.

The financial information with respect to Spire included in the Rule 2.7 Announcement and the Scheme Document has been or will have been prepared in accordance with accounting standards applicable in the UK and may not therefore be comparable to the financial information of US companies or companies whose financial statements are prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the US. Generally accepted accounting principles in the US differ in certain significant respects from the accounting standards applicable in the UK.

If, in the future, Bidco exercises its right to implement the Acquisition by way of a Takeover Offer and determines to extend the Takeover Offer into the US, the Acquisition will be made in compliance with applicable US laws and regulations, including Section 14(e) of the US Exchange Act and Regulation 14E thereunder.

The Acquisition herein is expected to have tax consequences for US Spire Shareholders. The receipt of the Cash Consideration as consideration for the transfer of Scheme Shares pursuant to the Scheme will be a taxable transaction for US federal income tax purposes. While Spire believes that it is not a passive foreign investment company (a "PFIC") for US federal income tax purposes for its current taxable year, no opinion has been obtained by Spire in this regard, and the determination of PFIC status is a factual one made annually after the close of the taxable year. Accordingly, there can be no assurance that Spire will not be treated as a PFIC for any taxable year. If Spire were a PFIC in any year while a US Spire Shareholder has owned Scheme Shares, any gain recognised on the transfer of its Scheme Shares pursuant to the Scheme generally would be ordinary income and an additional interest charge may apply if the Scheme Shares have been held for more than one taxable year.

US Spire Shareholders should read Part VIII of the Scheme Document which contains a description of certain US federal income tax consequences of the Scheme for US Spire Shareholders. US Spire Shareholders should be aware that the transaction contemplated herein may also have tax consequences for US federal income tax purposes and under applicable US state and local, as well as foreign and other, tax laws that are not described herein. Spire Shareholders (including US Spire Shareholders) are urged to consult with appropriate legal, tax and financial advisers in connection with the consequences of the Acquisition (including the Alternative Offer) on them.

Any Rollover Securities to be issued (subject to the implementation of the Rollover) pursuant to the Acquisition have not been and will not be registered under the US Securities Act or under the relevant securities laws of any state or territory or other jurisdiction of the United States. Accordingly, the Rollover Securities may not be offered, sold or delivered, directly or indirectly, in or into the US.

Neither the SEC nor any US state securities commission has approved or disapproved or passed judgment upon the fairness or the merits of the Acquisition or determined if this announcement is adequate, accurate or complete. Any representation to the contrary is a criminal offence in the US.

Each of Spire and Bidco is incorporated under the laws of England and Wales. In addition, some or all of their respective officers and directors reside outside the US, and some or all of their respective assets are or may be located in jurisdictions outside the US. Therefore, investors may have difficulty effecting service of process within the US upon those persons or recovering against Spire or Bidco or their respective officers or directors on judgments of US courts, including judgments based upon the civil liability provisions of US federal securities laws. Further, it may be difficult to compel a non-US company and its affiliates to subject themselves to a US court's judgment. It may be difficult for US Spire Shareholders to enforce their rights and claims arising out of the US federal securities law and it may not be possible to sue Spire or Bidco or their respective officers or directors in a non-US court for violations of US securities laws.

In accordance with normal United Kingdom practice and pursuant to Rule 14e-5(b) of the US Exchange Act, to the extent applicable, Bidco or its nominees or brokers (acting as agents) may from time to time make certain purchases of, or arrangements to purchase, Spire Shares outside the US, other than pursuant to the Acquisition, until the date on which the Acquisition becomes Effective, lapses or is otherwise withdrawn, in compliance with applicable law, including the US Exchange Act. These purchases may occur either in the open market at prevailing prices or in private transactions at negotiated prices. Any information about such purchases will be disclosed as required in the United Kingdom, will be reported via a Regulatory Information Service and will be available on the London Stock Exchange website at: http://www.londonstockexchange.com.

Disclosure requirements of the Code

Under Rule 8.3(a) of the Code, any person who is interested in 1% or more of any class of relevant securities of an offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror (being any offeror other than an offeror in respect of which it has been announced that its offer is, or is likely to be, solely in cash) must make an Opening Position Disclosure following the commencement of the offer period and, if later, following the announcement in which any securities exchange offeror is first identified.

An Opening Position Disclosure must contain details of the person’s interests and short positions in, and rights to subscribe for, any relevant securities of each of (i) the offeree company and (ii) any securities exchange offeror(s). An Opening Position Disclosure by a person to whom Rule 8.3(a) applies must be made by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the 10th business day following the commencement of the offer period and, if appropriate, by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the 10th business day following the announcement in which any securities exchange offeror is first identified. Relevant persons who deal in the relevant securities of the offeree company or of a securities exchange offeror prior to the deadline for making an Opening Position Disclosure must instead make a Dealing Disclosure.

Under Rule 8.3(b) of the Code, any person who is, or becomes, interested in 1% or more of any class of relevant securities of the offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror must make a Dealing Disclosure if the person deals in any relevant securities of the offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror. A Dealing Disclosure must contain details of the dealing concerned and of the person’s interests and short positions in, and rights to subscribe for, any relevant securities of each of (i) the offeree company and (ii) any securities exchange offeror(s), save to the extent that these details have previously been disclosed under Rule 8. A Dealing Disclosure by a person to whom Rule 8.3(b) applies must be made by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the business day following the date of the relevant dealing.

If two or more persons act together pursuant to an agreement or understanding, whether formal or informal, to acquire or control an interest in relevant securities of an offeree company or a securities exchange offeror, they will be deemed to be a single person for the purpose of Rule 8.3.

Opening Position Disclosures must also be made by the offeree company and by any offeror and Dealing Disclosures must also be made by the offeree company, by any offeror and by any persons acting in concert with any of them (see Rules 8.1, 8.2 and 8.4).

Details of the offeree and offeror companies in respect of whose relevant securities Opening Position Disclosures and Dealing Disclosures must be made can be found in the Disclosure Table on the Takeover Panel’s website at www.thetakeoverpanel.org.uk, including details of the number of relevant securities in issue, when the offer period commenced and when any offeror was first identified. You should contact the Panel’s Market Surveillance Unit on +44 (0)20 7638 0129 if you are in any doubt as to whether you are required to make an Opening Position Disclosure or a Dealing Disclosure.

data.title: Dollar set for fourth weekly gain, supported by Fed tightening expectations, AI-driven haven bid
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dollar index near strongest since early April 2025
  • Markets debating size, not likelihood, of December Fed hike
  • Yen firms after Japanese core inflation hits 2.2%

By Sophie Kiderlin

The dollar was steady on Friday and was on track to rise for the fourth straight week as expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening underpinned the US currency and jitters over the AI trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets.

The dollar index was perched near the 103.9 level, around its strongest since early April 2025. The weeks-long rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point hike in December should be considered.

The dollar was also supported by a reduced appetite for risk, with a multitude of AI-related concerns weighing on global stocks. Anthropic's record market debut on Thursday did little to revive investor confidence.

MSCI's world index of stocks fell for a seventh straight session EURONEXT:IACWI on Friday, the longest losing streak since 2023.

Chris Turner, global head of markets at ING, said that while there is only a weak case for another steep correction in equities, "there is no reason for the Fed to drop its hawkish rhetoric anytime soon."

He pointed to next week's US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, a key inflation gauge for the Fed, which Turner said will likely confirm that the Fed needs to act.

"For FX, that means a continued strong dollar and continued pressure on popular carry trades," he said.

In FX carry trades, investors borrow in low-yielding currencies, such as the Japanese yen and Swiss franc, to fund purchases of higher-yielding assets elsewhere, often in emerging markets.

Adding to the hawkish-leaning narrative, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the evidence did not suggest inflation was heading back to 2% on its own.

"The debate now is not really about whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December, but how much it will raise rates by," Carol Kong, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said.

"We still think 25 basis points is more likely," Kong added. "If they really want to quicken the pace of tightening, I think they will prefer to increase rates by 25 bps in consecutive meetings rather than deliver a bigger-than-usual hike."

Sterling languished near a one-year low against the dollar at $1.3105, and the euro struggled near its lowest level since April 2025 and last bought $1.0961.

YEN FIRMS ON INFLATION DATA

The yen firmed 0.6% against the dollar to 158.78 and is set to close the week with a small gain after three weeks of losses that had dragged the currency to near the key 160 level.

Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that strengthen the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

Analysts at Capital Economics argue the yen's recent weakness is unlikely to last. With long-term inflation expectations now around target, further increases in yields would be mostly in real terms, which, combined with their view that US yields will fall, should prove yen-positive, the analysts said.

ING's Turner also noted that a carry trade unwind should be a slight positive for the yen.

data.title: White House Reportedly Replaces Cyber Director Sean Cairncross Amid Widespread US Tech Outages
data.description:
Key points:
  • Kirsten Davies, a former technology and cybersecurity executive at Unilever, Estée Lauder and Hewlett Packard, will serve as acting cyber director.
  • Cairncross was confirmed by the Senate in August 2025 and previously led the Millennium Challenge Corporation.
  • The White House said it sees “no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity, or malign actor” behind the recent tech outages.

The White House has reportedly replaced National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross, following a series of major technology outages across the U.S.

Cairncross was no longer with the administration, Bloomberg reported, citing a White House official. A person familiar with the matter told the publication that he had been dismissed and Davies would replace him in an acting capacity.

A permanent national cyber director must first be nominated by the president and then confirmed by the Senate.

Cairncross, who was confirmed by the Senate in August 2025, previously served as a senior adviser to the White House chief of staff during Trump's first term and led the Millennium Challenge Corporation, Bloomberg reported.

White House Cyber Leadership Change

President Donald Trump's chief of staff, Stephen Miller, pushed for Cairncross's removal, two White House officials told Axios, with one official saying he “lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job.”

Davies previously held technology and cybersecurity roles at Unilever, Estée Lauder and Hewlett Packard, according to Bloomberg. Davies thanked Trump and Miller for their confidence in her.

“Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come …but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on, as well as build cyber talent for our future. Under President Trump’s leadership, we will have a more secure, resilient, and supercharged technological future, she wrote on X.

Tech Outages Affect Aviation, Microsoft, Government Systems

The leadership change comes after several major technology disruptions, including a nationwide aviation ground stop, a worldwide Microsoft (MSFT) Outlook outage and a reported blackout of the National Security Agency's classified communications network.

The White House said Wednesday, “The Trump Administration sees no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity, or malign actor behind the recent tech outages.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio also told reporters in Manila on Wednesday that the U.S. had no indication or evidence that the disruptions were connected or resulted from hostile acts, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: India meets ethanol blending goal as corn, rice boost supplies, industry body data shows
data.description:
India achieved its target of blending 20% ethanol with petrol in the 2025/26 supply year, as higher production of the biofuel from corn and rice lifted the average blending rate, an industry body said on Friday.

The average blending rate reached 19.99%, up from 19.24% a year earlier, with 11.34 billion litres of ethanol blended with petrol during the year ended October 31, the All India Distillers' Association said.

Corn-based ethanol accounted for a record 46% of total supplies, lifting the share of grain-based ethanol to 76%. Sugarcane-based feedstocks made up the remaining 24%, the association said.

However, ethanol blending could fall short of the government's 20% target in the supply year that began this month, industry insiders said, with the lowest monsoon rainfall in more than a decade threatening corn and sugarcane crops and forcing New Delhi to prioritise food security over ethanol production.

data.title: Deutsche Bank leaks add spice to succession debate
data.description:
By Neil Unmack

A 15-mln-document dump outlines how the €56 bln bank accidentally forwarded Donald Trump’s tax return, and other missteps. It’s mostly old news. But Deutsche's shares have dipped, and it raises the question of what happens after CEO Christian Sewing's mandate ends in 2029.

Full view will be published shortly.

Follow @Unmack1 on X

CONTEXT NEWS

The Financial Times this week published a series of articles based on leaks of internal documents at Deutsche Bank. The leaks, which were reviewed by over 200 journalists from publications including Der Spiegel and Le Monde, include revelations that Deutsche accidentally forwarded Donald Trump’s tax return to a third party, without disclosing it had done so.

The documents also list about $582 million in transactions linked to Jeffery Epstein, which were flagged internally as suspicious. Internal emails indicate that senior executives approved Epstein as a client despite his conviction, and kept his accounts open even after warnings about the activities of Ghislaine Maxwell, his former girlfriend and associate.

“The matters which are in focus of the media reports date back many years and in some cases as much as two decades," Deutsche said in a statement. “Where relevant, we reviewed these matters at the time and worked closely with regulators.”

Deutsche said it had invested €7 billion in its controls between 2019 and 2025, adding that “we are a different, stronger and safer bank today”.

Deutsche Bank shares were trading at €29 as of 0930 GMT on November 20, down over 10% since the start of the week.

data.title: The Logistics Report: Union Pacific CEO Apologizes as March Remark Fuels Opposition to Merger — WSJ Newsletter
data.description:
By Mark R. Long

Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena apologized for saying at a conference in March that he would raise rates for customers who don't support the merger of his railroad with Norfolk Southern.

"If I had to do it again, I wouldn't have said it," Vena said Thursday during a panel at the RailTrends conference in New York.

The Wall Street Journal's Esther Fung writes that Vena is trying to gather support for the $72 billion deal, which would create the first transcontinental U.S. railroad with a single operator. Proponents say the deal would cut shipping times and take less-efficient trucks off highways. Opponents, however, argue that competition will decrease and shippers will be worse off with fewer rail options.

In March, Vena said he would raise rates for shippers who don't support the merger, "to teach you a lesson." Vena's comments were mentioned or alluded to in several comments that opponents of the merger filed with the Surface Transportation Board, which is reviewing the deal, TrainsPRO reports.

On Thursday, Vena repeated that (Union Pacific) doesn't retaliate against customers and that the railroad was open to discussions with concerned shippers.

"It was my attempt at humor. I made a mistake."Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena

Retail

Walmart said its quarterly revenue rose 5.2%, with sales and profit from e-commerce, advertising and other newer businesses growing while in-store sales slid. The retail giant raised its financial guidance for the full year, and said comparable sales from stores and digital channels grew 2.9%, the WSJ's Sarah Nassauer writes.

Its most recent U.S. sales were helped by market-share gains in its food business, but hurt by pricing regulation in its pharmacy business. The retailer's global e-commerce sales grew by 17% and 23% in the U.S. Its U.S. advertising business was up 37%. E-commerce now accounts for around a quarter of (Walmart's) total sales.

Walmart also said it was using its online-ordering infrastructure to make more fast-food deliveries along with groceries and other products. David Guggina, CEO of Walmart U.S., said these restaurant deliveries helped strengthen the company's last-mile network, and that it was looking at other ways to expand delivery capabilities.

Number of the Day

$7,026

Average rate to ship a 40-foot container from Shanghai to Los Angeles in the week ended Nov. 19, down 5% from the previous week to its lowest in about three months, according to Drewry's World Container Index

Critical Materials

A U.S.-led consortium won the right to explore a major rare-earth deposit on Kenya's Indian Ocean coast, advancing the Trump administration's push to reduce reliance on China for the critical minerals, the WSJ's Caroline Kimeu reports.

Frontier Minerals, a consortium that includes two Indiana-based companies-American Resources Corp. and ReElement Technologies-as well as Idaho-based Bunker Hill Mining Group, beat out rivals for the license after a more than six-month competition. Two Chinese companies withdrew before the final bids, with no public explanation.

The deposits, which a previous license holder estimated to be worth around $62 billion, lie beneath Mrima Hill, a forested mound in Kenya's coastal Kwale county. The area also contains niobium, which is used in jet engines.

  • Logistics companies have been flooded with inquiries to ship copper to China from U.S. stockpiles, in a reversal of the past two years' buildup of American inventories of the metal. (Bloomberg)

In Other News

  • The Senate passed a bipartisan bill designed to speed up energy, mining and other infrastructure projects, overcoming concerns it would weaken environmental protection laws. (WSJ)
  • The number of Americans who filed for unemployment benefits unexpectedly rose to 203,000 in the week through Nov. 14. (WSJ)
  • Canada's industrial product price index rose 0.3% in October from September, driven by higher energy prices. (WSJ)
  • Procter & Gamble said it plans to cut 20% to 30% of its product-supply jobs by 2030, as it implements more automation into its supply chain. (WSJ)
  • The Chinese owner of bargain-shopping app Temu posted flat earnings as it continued to deal with subdued consumer sentiment at home and regulatory pressures abroad. (WSJ)
  • Deutsche Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 full-time jobs at its flagship airline's Frankfurt and Munich hubs. (WSJ)
  • Nestle is working with tech companies including Microsoft and Boston Dynamics to increase the use of AI in its factories and products. (WSJ)
  • GCM Grosvenor is backing Blue Yonder Property Group's strategy targeting manufacturing facilities with high capacity power infrastructure in place, potentially investing as much as $300 million. (WSJ)
  • Amazon said a proposed New York City law requiring the e-commerce giant to directly employ delivery workers could add up to $5 an order. (WSJ)
  • The Department of Labor announced a final rule that would more easily allow companies to categorize gig workers as independent contractors. (Bloomberg Law)
  • The United Steelworkers union said it reached a tentative four-year contract deal with Nippon Steel's U.S. Steel for workers at 13 facilities. (Pittsburgh Post-Gazette)
  • The Trump administration leased 31.5 million acres of Pacific Ocean floor to deep-sea-mining company Wetstone U.S. Ventures, in the first sale of its kind. (New York Times)
  • Panama's comptroller general filed a criminal complaint seeking a probe into possible crimes linked to an audit of the country's port-concession contract with a unit of Hong Kong's CK Hutchison. (Reuters)
  • U.S. sales of Class 8 heavy-duty trucks rose 59.6% year over year to 23,441 in October, according to Omdia Automotive. (Transport Topics)

data.title: AI Stocks Tumble Across the Globe as Slowdown Fears Mount
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Artificial intelligence stocks fell across the globe as sentiment around the AI trade deteriorated further, despite Anthropic's record-breaking IPO Thursday.

Nasdaq futures were 1.3% lower as the index headed toward its worst one-week performance since President Trump's April 2025 imposition of sweeping tariffs. Chip makers and cloud-computing stocks sold off. Intel and Micron Technology fell 4.5% and 5.2% premarket, respectively, while Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 6.2%, extending a sharp fall from the last session following a short-seller report into the company published Thursday. Stocks that benefit from the build-out in AI suffered too, with data center power-supplier Caterpillar down 2.5% premarket.

Tech giants that served as havens in previous AI wobbles provided no safety premarket, with Meta Platforms and Microsoft both falling more than 1%.

So-called Animal spirits are taking over the market, XTB's Kathleen Brooks said. Multiple fears are weighing on investors' outlook, the research director said, including worries about high financing costs, excessive AI spending and legislation that could hurt the technology in the U.S.

Combined, those factors threaten a pullback in the AI build-out that could lead to lower revenues for related companies.

Asian stocks were hit hard Friday. South Korean memory-chip makers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell 7% and 5.9%, respectively. In Japan, SoftBank Group--a major backer of OpenAI--fell 14.5%.

Europe's most valuable company, Dutch supplier of chip-making equipment ASML, fell close to 6%, putting it on track to lose around 28 billion euros of market value ($30.71 billion). A gauge of the continent's tech sector fell 3.6%.

Anthropic itself was down more than 6.5% premarket to trade around $90.80 a share. Adding to pressure on the stock was news, first reported by Bloomberg, that Apple is developing a new autonomous AI agent. The consumer-focused product could offer fresh competition to Anthropic's models.

Analysts are also concerned that Anthropic's revenue growth won't be enough to significantly outpace its spending commitments. The model maker has spending commitments totaling $900.9 billion, around half of which are due over the next five years, according to its IPO filing with the SEC.

"We are concerned about Anthropic's revenue growth," Seaport Research senior analyst Jay Goldberg wrote in a note. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years."

Investors are ditching AI stocks over fears that the sector's spending boom has passed its peak "in spite of a lack of any compelling evidence as yet of any such development on the ground," Jefferies' global head of equity strategy, Christopher Wood, said.

Driving the fear are concerns that Nvidia will step back from its role as financier-in-chief for the wider AI ecosystem, Wood said. In particular, investors worry Nvidia will pull its backing of chip-hungry cloud-computing startups, Wood said.

"This suggests a real risk that the most speculative part of the demand for compute will disappear which should lower compute prices for others."

Write to Joe Stonor at josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com

data.title: BJ’s Wholesale Club Reports Q3 FY2026 Results; Raises Full-Year Outlook
data.description:
BJ’s Wholesale Club reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue of $6.28 billion, up 17.5% year over year, and diluted EPS of $1.73. Net income rose 44.4% to $219.5 million, while adjusted EBITDA increased 39.9% to $421.6 million. The company raised its full-year comparable sales and adjusted EPS outlook.

Financial Highlights

  • Total revenue was $6.28 billion, up 17.5% from $5.35 billion; net sales were $6.15 billion, up 17.7%.
  • Gross profit was approximately $1.02 billion, compared with $1.01 billion a year earlier. Merchandise gross margin rate, excluding gasoline sales and membership fee income, declined approximately 170 basis points, primarily due to promotional activity.
  • Operating income increased 43.7% to $313.8 million, compared with $218.4 million.
  • Net income increased 44.4% to $219.5 million. Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.73, compared with $1.16.
  • Fiscal 2026 guidance calls for adjusted EPS of $5.10 to $5.30 and capital expenditures of approximately $800 million.

Business Highlights

  • Comparable club sales increased 13.5% in the quarter; excluding gasoline, comparable sales grew 4.1%.
  • Digitally enabled comparable sales grew 38%, with two-year stacked growth of 69%.
  • Membership acquisition, retention and higher-tier membership penetration contributed to record membership.
  • The company opened two clubs and five gas stations during the quarter.
  • The company repurchased 376,942 shares in the quarter; approximately $386.9 million remained available under its share repurchase program.

Original SEC Filing: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. [ BJ ] - 8-K - Nov. 20, 2026

data.title: What European investors think of the US AI trade
data.description:
Key points:
  • Stoxx 600 down 1.2%, volatility at highest since April
  • European tech index down 3.6% on day, 8.9% on week
  • Tech set for biggest weekly fall since late 2020
  • Asia ex Japan shares post biggest weekly fall since 2020
  • US futures lower, VIX above 30

WHAT EUROPEAN INVESTORS THINK OF THE US AI TRADE

While stock markets stumble around the world on Friday after Anthropic's IPO failed to reignite the rally in the AI sector, a rundown of European investors' concerns could come in handy.

According to a UBS report based on investor meetings across Europe, “some clients argued that the recent technology sell-off looks partly technical rather than fundamental, with de-grossing in AI and semiconductors potentially offering a better entry point.”

"With defensives not cheap, a further rotation away from AI was not seen as compelling," the UBS report says.

“Some clients said that they would like to see some further performance of fixed income before reallocating into it, especially given expectations of further AI debt issuance.”

A bond price rise triggers a fall in borrowing costs, making debt issuance cheaper.

China could also become an issue.

“US AI leadership remains powerful, but we heard that the market may be underestimating Chinese competition and the potential fragmentation of corporate demand."

“The question is not just how quickly AI capex grows, but who will own the infrastructure, control the data and capture the monetization,” the UBS report adds.

(Stefano Rebaudo)

data.title: Anthropic's stock surges in its debut - and the rest of the market dives anyway
data.description:
By Joy Wiltermuth and Joseph Adinolfi

All four major U.S. stock indexes are now on pace for their worst week since President Trump's 'liberation day' tariffs of April 2025

The stock market is convulsing despite a hugely successful IPO from Anthropic on Thursday.

Neither a wildly successful first-ever IPO from an artificial-intelligence lab, nor a blockbuster earnings report from arguably the most important company in the AI trade, were enough to stop the carnage in the U.S. stock market this week.

Earlier this week, Nvidia (NVDA) passed a big "earnings test" after the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang - but its stock fell anyway. Then, on Thursday, Anthropic's (ANT) hugely anticipated IPO passed the market's next big "valuation test," with the AI lab's stock opening 34% above its $83 IPO price, before it closed at $97.17.

Yet the S&P 500 index SPX still tumbled 2% Thursday to close at 7,175.83, as a broad-based selloff left each of the index's 11 sectors in the red for a second time in three days, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

"I'm a bit surprised that we are cascading here," said Mark Arbeter, president of Arbeter Investments. He expected Nivida's earnings and Anthropic's successful IPO to calm the market, allow it to bottom "at least on a short-term basis" and open the door to "a decent snapback rally."

Instead, the S&P 500 stayed below its 200-day moving average, a crucial support level, and was edging closer to the 7,000 mark. Any close below 7,037.04 would officially land the S&P 500 in a correction, or a drop of at least 10% from its previous peak, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

To be sure, corrections of 10% are considered normal, and the stock market isn't the U.S. economy, which lately has been showing signs of speeding up.

"Technically, it's been a long time since we've had a significant downturn in the market, and I think we are due," said David Kelly, chief global strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management. "I don't think it's much more than that."

Kelly doesn't think "the amount of money raised by Anthropic sucked the market dry." Instead, if there's any problem, it's that people's portfolios have become overly concentrated, he said. Furthermore, he thinks nothing about the economy's resilience has changed. "People should try to stay calm," he added.

Still, while past dips in stocks were bought, now there appears to be "a lot of loose hands holding equities right now," said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist at LPL Financial.

Lately, when stocks have opened higher, the market has failed to hold those gains through the close. Turnquist noted. "Sentiment has clearly changed in the market," he said.

To put a finer point on the scope of Thursday's selloff, only 38 stocks in the S&P 500 rose on Thursday - the fewest since Dec. 31, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The heavy losses had the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA down 6.2% for the week and teetering on the edge of correction territory.

The S&P 500 was off 5.1% for the week, while the Nasdaq Composite COMP was 5% lower and the Russell 2000 index RUT of small-cap stocks was off 4.9%. If those declines hold, it would be the worst week for all four indexes since the "liberation day" tariff selloff in the week of April 4, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

-Joy Wiltermuth -Joseph Adinolfi
